questions.question: How many job applicants had applied if the ratio of selected to unselected was 19 : 17. If 1,200 less had applied and 800 less selected, then the ratio of selected to unselected would have been 1 : 1.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio (Total : Selected) = 36 : 19 (since 19 + 17 = 36)

Final Ratio (Total : Selected) = 2 : 1 (since 1 : 1 means 1 out of 2 are selected)

Apply Cross-Product: |(36 × 1) − (19 × 2)| units = |(2 × 800) − (1 × 1200)|

|36 − 38| units = |1600 − 1200| ⇒ 2 units = 400

1 unit = 200 ∴ Initial Total = 36 × 200 = 7200

**∴ The correct answer is 7200 applicants.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selected : Unselected = 19 : 17

Reduction in Applied = 1200 | Reduction in Selected = 800

Final Selected : Unselected = 1 : 1

**Formula Used:**

Total Applicants = Selected + Unselected

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2114c1edc2c82a4221216a1f0c9e596f29b6f0a92de65a3a09aabbe91d28fab5.png] 

Let initial Selected = 19x and Unselected = 17x

⇒ Total Applicants = 19x + 17x = 36x

⇒ New Total Applicants = 36x − 1200

⇒ New Selected Applicants = 19x − 800

According to the new ratio (1 : 1), Selected = 1/2 of Total:

⇒ (19x − 800) = 1/2 × (36x − 1200)

⇒ 2 × (19x − 800) = 36x − 1200

⇒ 38x − 1600 = 36x − 1200

⇒ 38x − 36x = 1600 − 1200

⇒ 2x = 400

⇒ x = 200

⇒ Initial Applicants = 36 × 200 = 7200

**∴ The correct answer is 7200 applicants.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

The ratio of the products of the antecedents and the products of the consequents of two or more ratios. For a:b and c:d, it is (ac):(bd).

Componento and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a-b) = (c+d)/(c-d). This is useful in solving complex ratio equations involving additions or subtractions.

Cross-Multiplication Method

Used when an initial ratio is changed by adding/subtracting specific values to reach a final ratio. It avoids setting up full algebraic equations.</p

questions.question: What is the third proportional to 10 and 20?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a continued proportion a : b :: b : c, the third proportional c is calculated as b² ÷ a.

Given a = 10 and b = 20.

Third proportional = (20 × 20) ÷ 10 = 400 ÷ 10 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number (a) = 10, Second number (b) = 20.

**Formula Used:** If three numbers a, b, and c are in proportion, then a : b = b : c, where c is the third proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7c701c6fd10ad8d0563dbd981f3c82c9ddbb5e0e60b676d5c2f2535ad3a216b.png] 

⇒ Let the third proportional be c.

⇒ 10 : 20 = 20 : c

⇒ 10 ÷ 20 = 20 ÷ c

⇒ 10 × c = 20 × 20

⇒ 10c = 400

⇒ c = 400 ÷ 10

⇒ c = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is calculated as x = √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b = c : d, which gives d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion Property

Three non-zero numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to the second equals the ratio of the second to the third (a/b = b/c).</p

questions.question: The ratio of the sum of the salaries of A and B to the difference of their salaries is 11 : 1 and the ratio of the sum of the salaries of B and C to the difference of their salaries is also 11 : 1. If A's salary is the highest and C's is the lowest then what is B's salary (in Rs) given the total of all their salaries is Rs. 1,82,000?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By Componendo & Dividendo, if (S+D)/(S−D) = 11/1, then the ratio of terms is (11+1)/(11−1) = 12/10 = 6/5.

So, A : B = 6 : 5 and B : C = 6 : 5.

Combined ratio A : B : C = (6×6) : (5×6) : (5×5) = 36 : 30 : 25.

Total units = 36 + 30 + 25 = 91 units.

91 units = ₹1,82,000 → 1 unit = ₹2,000.

B's salary = 30 units × 2,000 = ₹60,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(A + B) / (A − B) = 11 / 1

(B + C) / (B − C) = 11 / 1

Total salary (A + B + C) = ₹1,82,000

**Formula Used:**

Componendo and Dividendo: If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e3f42d049db19d0cd131b8f5aeccbe7c27acf7b6af1a9858d54707c688a39eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

From (A + B) / (A − B) = 11 / 1:

⇒ Applying Componendo & Dividendo: ((A + B) + (A − B)) / ((A + B) − (A − B)) = (11 + 1) / (11 − 1)

⇒ 2A / 2B = 12 / 10

⇒ A / B = 6 / 5

Similarly, for B and C:

⇒ B / C = 6 / 5

To combine the ratios, make B common:

⇒ A : B = 6 : 5 = (6 × 6) : (5 × 6) = 36 : 30

⇒ B : C = 6 : 5 = (6 × 5) : (5 × 5) = 30 : 25

⇒ A : B : C = 36 : 30 : 25

Sum of ratio parts:

⇒ 36 + 30 + 25 = 91 units

⇒ 91 units = ₹1,82,000

⇒ 1 unit = 1,82,000 ÷ 91 = ₹2,000

Calculate B’s salary:

⇒ B = 30 × 2,000 = ₹60,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

It is a theorem on proportions that allows for quick calculation of individual variables when the ratio of their sum and difference is known. If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d).

Combined Ratio

When two ratios a : b and b : c are given, the combined ratio a : b : c can be found by making the common term 'b' equal in both ratios through multiplication.

Partitive Proportion

It involves dividing a total amount into parts based on a specific ratio. Value of one part = Total Amount ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts.

questions.question: If by increasing the price of a ticket in the ratio 8 : 11 the number of tickets sold fall in the ratio 23 : 21 then what is the increase (in Rs.) in revenue if revenue before increase in price of ticket was Rs. 36,800?

Revenue Ratio = (Initial Price × Initial Quantity) : (Final Price × Final Quantity)

Revenue Ratio = (8 × 23) : (11 × 21) = 184 : 231

Initial Revenue = 184 units = ₹36,800 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹200

Increase in Revenue = 231 − 184 = 47 units

Required Increase = 47 × 200 = ₹9,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Price : Final Price = 8 : 11

Initial Tickets : Final Tickets = 23 : 21

Initial Revenue = ₹36,800

**Formula Used:**

Revenue = Price × Number of Tickets Sold

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0dbcb8613e62bb753ea9e0607135833470c814b5d9b1734ac3671ddf3c0959f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let initial price = 8x and initial quantity = 23y

⇒ Initial Revenue = 8x × 23y = 184xy

⇒ Final Price = 11x and final quantity = 21y

⇒ Final Revenue = 11x × 21y = 231xy

⇒ Given: 184xy = 36800

⇒ xy = 36800 ÷ 184 = 200

⇒ Increase in revenue = Final Revenue − Initial Revenue

⇒ Increase = 231xy − 184xy = 47xy

⇒ Increase = 47 × 200 = ₹9,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Ratios

When a quantity depends on the product of two independent variables (like Revenue = Price × Quantity), the ratio of the new quantity to the old is the product of the individual ratios of those variables.

Percentage Change in Product

If one factor increases by a% and the other increases by b%, the net percentage change in the product is given by the formula: [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Compounding Ratios

To find the combined effect of two ratios a:b and c:d, we multiply them as (a×c):(b×d). This is known as compounding the ratios.

questions.question: The ratio of ages of the father and mother was 11 ∶ 10 when their son was born. The ratio of ages of the father and mother will be 19 ∶ 18 when the son will be twice his present age. What is the ratio of present ages of father and mother?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio at son's birth (Son = 0) → 11 : 10 (Difference = 1 unit)

Ratio at Son = 2x years → 19 : 18 (Difference = 1 unit)

Since the difference is same, total growth in 2x years = 19 − 11 = 8 units.

Growth for present age (x years) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 units.

Present ratio = (11 + 4) : (10 + 4) = 15 : 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 14.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio (Son = 0) = 11 : 10

Future ratio (Son = 2 × present age) = 19 : 18

**Formula Used:**

Age = Initial age + time elapsed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1647c10847b096ec779c95aeca941664d48528f74051b8d4f6ac57c95007f6ed.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the ages of father and mother at son's birth be 11k and 10k.

Let the son's present age be x.

Ages at the time when son will be 2x years old:

Father's age = 11k + 2x

Mother's age = 10k + 2x

⇒ (11k + 2x) ÷ (10k + 2x) = 19 ÷ 18

⇒ 18 × (11k + 2x) = 19 × (10k + 2x)

⇒ 198k + 36x = 190k + 38x

⇒ 198k − 190k = 38x − 36x

⇒ 8k = 2x

⇒ x = 4k

Present ages:

Father = 11k + x = 11k + 4k = 15k

Mother = 10k + x = 10k + 4k = 14k

⇒ Ratio = 15k : 14k = 15 : 14

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 14.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people always remains the same, regardless of the number of years passed. In ratio problems, always try to equalize this difference.

Ratio Scaling

If the difference between two ratios a:b and c:d is not the same, multiply (a:b) by (d−c) and (c:d) by (b−a) to make the differences equal.

Linear Increment

When everyone in a group grows by 'n' years, their total age increases by (number of people × n) and the average age increases by exactly n years.</p

questions.question: Of the 3 numbers whose average is 22, the first is 3/8th the sum of other two. What is the first number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of 3 numbers = 22 × 3 = 66.

Ratio of the 1st number to the sum of the other two = 3 : 8.

Total ratio parts = 3 + 8 = 11 units.

11 units = 66 ⇒ 1 unit = 6.

First number = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Average of 3 numbers = 22.

Condition: 1st number = 3/8 × (Sum of other two).

Formula: Sum = Average × Number of items.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99292d0cabd2d8d7cafff884bb2aea662e05634492a683710f950b1c18a64677.png] 

⇒ Let the three numbers be x, y, and z.

⇒ (x + y + z) ÷ 3 = 22

⇒ x + y + z = 22 × 3 = 66

⇒ Given: x = 3/8 × (y + z)

⇒ 8x = 3(y + z) ⇒ (y + z) = 8x/3

⇒ Substitute (y + z) in the sum equation:

⇒ x + 8x/3 = 66

⇒ (3x + 8x) / 3 = 66

⇒ 11x / 3 = 66

⇒ 11x = 198

⇒ x = 198 ÷ 11 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

Average is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Average = ∑x / n.

Ratio and Proportion

If a total quantity S is divided into two parts in the ratio a:b, the first part is [a / (a + b)] × S and the second part is [b / (a + b)] × S.

Sum of Observations

The total sum of n observations can always be found by multiplying the average by n. Sum = Average × n.</p

questions.question: The average of three consecutive odd numbers is 52 more than 1/3rd of the largest of these numbers. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of three consecutive odd numbers is the middle number.

Let the middle number be M. The largest number is M + 2.

Given: M = (1/3) × (M + 2) + 52

3M = M + 2 + 156 ⇒ 2M = 158 ⇒ M = 79.

Smallest number = M − 2 = 79 − 2 = 77.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three consecutive odd numbers. The average is 52 more than 1/3rd of the largest number.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf9e9de0a86b40e800519cf3a7eeae72575ff4b8b9fb80078542688f29589302.png] 

Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, x + 2, and x + 4.

⇒ Average = (x + x + 2 + x + 4) ÷ 3

⇒ Average = (3x + 6) ÷ 3 = x + 2

According to the problem:

⇒ x + 2 = (1/3) × (x + 4) + 52

⇒ 3(x + 2) = (x + 4) + (52 × 3)

⇒ 3x + 6 = x + 4 + 156

⇒ 3x + 6 = x + 160

⇒ 3x − x = 160 − 6

⇒ 2x = 154

⇒ x = 77

The smallest number is x = 77.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any arithmetic progression with an odd number of terms, the average is exactly the middle term: Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Properties of Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a common difference of 2. The sum of n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is given by n².

Average Change Rule

If each number in a set is increased by a constant k, the average also increases by k. If multiplied by k, the average is multiplied by k.</p

questions.question: A batsman scores 98 runs in the 17th match of his career. His average runs per match increased by 2.5. What is his average before the 17th match?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total matches played including the current one = 17

Increase in average = 2.5

Total increase in runs across all 17 matches = 17 × 2.5 = 42.5

Old average (Average before 17th match) = Score in 17th match − Total increase

Old average = 98 − 42.5 = 55.5

**∴ The correct answer is 55.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Runs in 17th match = 98

Increase in average = 2.5

**Formula:**

Average = (Total Runs) ÷ (Number of Matches)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa09045fb51711e0b939dd1cb23d81e35ddafb4bf13f9c7f73d7c4253935ad81.png] 

Let the average before 17th match be x.

Total runs after 16 matches = 16x

Total runs after 17 matches = 16x + 98

New average after 17 matches = x + 2.5

⇒ (16x + 98) ÷ 17 = x + 2.5

⇒ 16x + 98 = 17(x + 2.5)

⇒ 16x + 98 = 17x + 42.5

⇒ 17x − 16x = 98 − 42.5

⇒ x = 55.5

**∴ The correct answer is 55.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

New Average Formula

New Average = Old Average + (Increase in Average) = 55.5 + 2.5 = 58.

Weighted Average Concept

If an observation is added, New Sum = (Old Average × Old n) + New Observation. The change in average is (New Observation − Old Average) ÷ New n.

Score Calculation

Score of the nth match = New Average + (n − 1) × (Increase in Average).

**∴ The correct answer is 55.5.**</p

questions.question: What is the average of all numbers between 100 and 200 which are divisible by 13?

Last number divisible by 13 before 200 = 13 × 15 = 195.

**∴ The correct answer is 149.5.**

**Given:** Numbers between 100 and 200 divisible by 13.

**Formula Used:** Average of Arithmetic Progression = (a + l) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5b4dfb62f23366c0d9338fad0709404e9dfc9802e6c73d16cf2180294460785.png] 

⇒ Multiples of 13 in the range: 13 × 8, 13 × 9, ..., 13 × 15.

⇒ The series is: 104, 117, 130, 143, 156, 169, 182, 195.

⇒ First term (a) = 104.

⇒ Last term (l) = 195.

⇒ Average = (104 + 195) ÷ 2.

⇒ Average = 299 ÷ 2 = 149.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 149.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of AP Sequence

The average of any sequence in Arithmetic Progression is always the arithmetic mean of the first and last terms, i.e., Average = (a + l) ÷ 2.

Number of Terms in AP

The number of terms 'n' can be calculated using n = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1.

Sum of AP Terms

The sum of terms in an AP is given by Sₙ = n × Average = (n ÷ 2) × [First Term + Last Term].</p

questions.question: A vendor buys 9 bananas for Rs. 8 and sells 8 for Rs. 9. What will be the profit or loss (in %)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the cross-multiplication method for Article vs Price:

CP: 9 articles for ₹8 | SP: 8 articles for ₹9

Cross-multiply: (9 × 9) − (8 × 8) = 81 − 64 = 17 (Profit units)

Profit % = (Difference ÷ Product of inner values) × 100

Profit % = (17 ÷ 64) × 100 = 26.5625% ≈ 26.56%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.56% profit.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Cost Price (CP) of 9 bananas = ₹8

Selling Price (SP) of 8 bananas = ₹9

To find profit or loss, we equalize the quantity of bananas by taking the LCM of 9 and 8 (LCM = 72).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9fa729562ff6bb9458f67a1b5bba1b92952b310a67a0983dac33586041370a85.png] 

⇒ CP of 1 banana = 8 ÷ 9

⇒ SP of 1 banana = 9 ÷ 8

⇒ Total CP for 72 bananas = (8 ÷ 9) × 72 = ₹64

⇒ Total SP for 72 bananas = (9 ÷ 8) × 72 = ₹81

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 81 − 64 = ₹17

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (17 ÷ 64) × 100 = 26.5625%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.56% profit.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentages

Profit % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method for Articles

When quantities are different, find the price of 1 unit or use the LCM of quantities to make them equal for direct comparison.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP): SP = MP − Discount. Effective profit is then calculated from SP and CP.

Direct Ratio: SP₁ ÷ (100 − Loss%) = SP₂ ÷ (100 + Profit%)

2.5 = SP₂ ÷ 110

SP₂ = 2.5 × 110 = 275

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹200

Loss Percentage = 20%

Desired Profit Percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

questions.question: A wholesaler had 200 dozens of mangoes. He sold some of these mangoes at 20% profit and the rest at 10% profit, so that he made 13% profit on selling all the mangoes. How many mangoes (in dozens) did he sell at 20% profit?

Total units = 3 + 7 = 10 units → 200 dozens.

Mangoes at 20% profit = 3 units = (200 ÷ 10) × 3 = 60 dozens.

⇒ Let the quantity sold at 20% profit be Q₁ and at 10% profit be Q₂.

⇒ By Alligation Rule: Q₁ : Q₂ = (13 − 10) : (20 − 13)

⇒ Q₁ : Q₂ = 3 : 7

⇒ Total ratio parts = 3 + 7 = 10 units

⇒ 10 units = 200 dozens

⇒ 1 unit = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 dozens

⇒ Quantity at 20% profit = 3 × 20 dozens

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices/percentages must be mixed to produce a mixture at a given mean price/percentage. Formula: (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (CP of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − CP of Cheaper).

questions.question: If the selling price is tripled and the cost price is doubled, the profit would become 65%. What is the present profit (in %)?

questions.question: When a number is increased by 216, it becomes 140% of itself. What is the number?

The number becomes 140% of itself, meaning the increase is 40%.

Given that this 40% increase corresponds to the value 216.

40% of Number = 216

100% of Number = (216 ÷ 40) × 100 = 5.4 × 100 = 540

**∴ The correct answer is 540.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in number = 216

New value = 140% of the original number

**Formula Used:**

New Value = Original Value + Increase

**Calculations:**

Let the original number be x.

⇒ x + 216 = 140% of x

⇒ x + 216 = (140 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ x + 216 = 1.4x

⇒ 1.4x − x = 216

⇒ 0.4x = 216

⇒ x = 216 ÷ 0.4

⇒ x = 2160 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 540

**∴ The correct answer is 540.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Original Value) × 100. In this case, 40 = (216 ÷ x) × 100.

Fractional Equivalents

Base Value Concept

questions.question: A man donates 30% of his wealth to charity. 30% and 25% of the remaining wealth to his wife and son respectively. The rest he divides equally among his three daughters. One of his daughter gets Rs. 42 lakh as her share. What was the man's wealth (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining wealth after charity = 100% − 30% = 70%.

Total share of Wife and Son from remaining = 30% + 25% = 55%.

Remaining for 3 daughters = 100% − 55% = 45% of the 70% wealth.

Share of one daughter = (45% ÷ 3) × 70% = 15% × 70% = 10.5%.

10.5% = 42 lakh ⇒ 100% = (42 ÷ 10.5) × 100 = 4 × 100 = 400 lakh.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400 lakhs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Charity donation = 30% of total wealth.

Wife's share = 30% of remaining wealth.

Son's share = 25% of remaining wealth.

One daughter's share = Rs. 42 lakh (shared equally among 3 daughters).

**Formula Used:**

Remaining Value = Initial Value × (100 − x)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e524e1a7ef3b06a04812c0473a5486a572f4a9667b37061ba83edd85e688c5d.png] 

Let total wealth be Rs. W lakhs.

⇒ Charity = 0.30 × W

⇒ Remaining Wealth (R₁) = W − 0.30W = 0.70W

⇒ Sum of Wife and Son's percentage of R₁ = 30% + 25% = 55%

⇒ Rest wealth for daughters = 100% − 55% = 45% of R₁

⇒ Total wealth for daughters = 0.45 × 0.70W = 0.315W

⇒ Wealth of one daughter = 0.315W ÷ 3 = 0.105W

⇒ Given: 0.105W = 42

⇒ W = 42 ÷ 0.105

⇒ W = 42000 ÷ 105

⇒ W = 400 lakhs

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400 lakhs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Deduction

When multiple deductions are made from the "remaining" amount, use the formula: Final = Initial × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100).

Simultaneous Deduction from Same Base

If multiple parts (like wife and son) are taken from the same "remaining" base, their percentages are added together before deduction (e.g., 30% + 25% = 55% of the remainder).

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

10.5% can be written as 10.5/100 = 21/200. If 21 units = 42, then 200 units = 400.</p

questions.question: A bus travels 720 km in 20 hours. Calculate its average speed in meters/second.

Speed in km/h = 720 ÷ 20 = 36 km/h

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total Distance = 720 km, Total Time = 20 hours

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1210eb71cc67bc361cb6c99b1b18f61539144846236731bfdb740341356cc71.png] 

⇒ Average Speed (km/h) = 720 ÷ 20

⇒ Average Speed (km/h) = 36 km/h

⇒ Since 1 km = 1000 m and 1 hour = 3600 s,

⇒ 1 km/h = 1000/3600 m/s = 5/18 m/s

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ Speed in m/s = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Factor

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed Formula

When a distance is covered at speed 'x' and the same distance is covered back at speed 'y', the average speed for the whole journey is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relationship between Speed, Distance, and Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Distance = Speed × Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed.</p

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 21 km/h and comes back the same distance at 28 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?

When the distance covered is the same for two different speeds, use the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 21 × 28) ÷ (21 + 28)

Average Speed = 1176 ÷ 49 = 24 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Upstream Speed (u) = 21 km/h, Downstream Speed (v) = 28 km/h.

⇒ Let the distance for one way be the LCM of 21 and 28, which is 84 km.

General Average Speed Formula

Boat Speed in Still Water

Speed of Stream

Average Speed for Equal Time

questions.question: Flight A usually takes 1 hour more than Flight B to travel a distance of 7200 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of flight B becomes 5/6 times of its actual speed, so it takes 36 minutes more than Flight A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Flight A (in km/hr)?

questions.question: An investor invested his saving in the stock market. The value of his investments increased by 12% and 9% in the first year and the second year respectively. If the value of his investments after two years became Rs. 97,664 then how much had he invested (in Rs.)?

questions.question: What is the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3 years is Rs. 6,000 and compound interest earned for 2 years is Rs. 4,160?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1 year = 6000 ÷ 3 = ₹2000.

SI for 2 years = 2000 × 2 = ₹4000.

CI for 2 years = ₹4160.

Difference (Interest on 1st year SI) = 4160 − 4000 = ₹160.

Rate (R%) = (160 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Simple Interest (SI) for 3 years = ₹6000, Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹4160.

Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI for 2 years = 2 × (SI for 1 year) + Interest on SI of 1st year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a99ab647b232928b3b65e484cc30fe1f93b02b33041eb28688bef67f1eabad5b.png] 

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 6000 ÷ 3 = ₹2000

⇒ Simple Interest for 2 years = 2000 × 2 = ₹4000

⇒ Compound Interest for 2 years = ₹4160

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 4160 − 4000 = ₹160

⇒ This difference (₹160) is the interest calculated on the SI of the first year (₹2000) for 1 year.

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Difference × 100) ÷ (SI for 1 year × Time)

⇒ R = (160 × 100) ÷ (2000 × 1)

⇒ R = 16000 ÷ 2000 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CI and SI for 2 Years

For a period of 2 years, the ratio of CI to SI is given by CI/SI = (200 + R)/200, where R is the annual rate of interest.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years can be calculated using the formula: D = P(R/100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

The difference (D) for 3 years is calculated as: D = [P(R/100)²] × [(300 + R)/100].

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest remains constant for every year if the principal and rate of interest do not change.

In the given figure, in ΔSTU, ST = 8 cm, TU = 9 cm and SU = 12 cm. QU = 24 cm, SR = 32 cm and PT = 27 cm. What is the ratio of the area of ΔPQU and area of ΔPTR?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a51d75f7a43473f64b8b86a47f64963ccf08aad0e6c1c159fb298cd77bcdd185.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From ΔSTU, using Sine Rule: sin U / sin T = ST / SU = 8 / 12 = 2/3.

Calculate extended segments: PU = PT − TU = 27 − 9 = 18 cm and TR = SR − ST = 32 − 8 = 24 cm.

Area Ratio = (PU × QU × sin U) / (PT × TR × sin T).

Ratio = (18 × 24 × sin U) / (27 × 24 × sin T) = (18 / 27) × (sin U / sin T) = 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: ST = 8 cm, TU = 9 cm, SU = 12 cm, QU = 24 cm, SR = 32 cm, PT = 27 cm.

Formula: Area of a triangle = 1/2 × a × b × sin(θ)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16b35d278a563c1424c3615b2312195badb0d843ccb19509842e20bc7275b350.png] 

⇒ In ΔSTU, by Law of Sines: ST / sin U = SU / sin T

⇒ sin U / sin T = ST / SU = 8 / 12 = 2/3

⇒ From the figure, P, U, T are collinear: PU = PT − TU = 27 − 9 = 18 cm

⇒ S, T, R are collinear: TR = SR − ST = 32 − 8 = 24 cm

⇒ Area(ΔPQU) = 1/2 × PU × QU × sin U = 1/2 × 18 × 24 × sin U

⇒ Area(ΔPTR) = 1/2 × PT × TR × sin T = 1/2 × 27 × 24 × sin T

⇒ Ratio = [1/2 × 18 × 24 × sin U] / [1/2 × 27 × 24 × sin T]

⇒ Ratio = (18 / 27) × (sin U / sin T) = 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Law of Sines

In any triangle, the ratio of a side to the sine of its opposite angle is constant: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

Area of Triangle (Sine Formula)

The area of a triangle can be calculated as 1/2 × a × b × sin C, where a and b are side lengths and C is the included angle.

Ratio of Areas of Triangles sharing an Angle

If two triangles share a common vertex and their bases are on the same lines, the ratio of their areas depends on the product of the lengths of the sides forming that angle and the sine of the angle.</p
